subject: Your MCP directories post
text:
Hi Apideck team,

I read your where to list your MCP server post and liked that you actually counted what each directory showed on Oct 31 instead of guessing. Really useful.

One gap for makers: a lot of MCP servers now ship as ChatGPT/Codex plugins, and PickAPlugin (https://pickaplugin.com) is a free, hand-sorted directory for those. No account needed to get listed, makers just email or submit the repo. If you ever refresh the post, it might be worth a line. Happy to list API Tracker's MCP server too if you'd like.

Aaron, PickAPlugin

subject: MCP server directories page
text:
Hi,

Your MCP server directories page is one of the more honest ones out there, especially the column on whether each listing's link is followed or nofollow.

Since you already cover OpenAI's plugin directory: PickAPlugin (https://pickaplugin.com) is an independent, free directory of ChatGPT and Codex plugins, and a lot of those bundle MCP servers. Listings are free and link straight to the repo. If you think it fits, I'd be glad to see it on the page next time you update it.

Aaron, PickAPlugin

subject: Your hosted MCP server listing post
text:
Hi Left Hook folks,

Enjoyed your post on where to list a hosted MCP server. The bit about Glama needing to come before awesome-remote saved me some confusion.

You mention ChatGPT submissions, so maybe this helps your readers: once a hosted server is wrapped as a ChatGPT/Codex plugin, it can also go on PickAPlugin (https://pickaplugin.com), a free, hand-sorted plugin directory. No fee, no account. Worth a mention if you update it.

Aaron, PickAPlugin

subject: Your MCP directories roundup
text:
Hi Linkly team,

I liked your MCP directories roundup, especially the 'what we listed, for the record' section. Rare to see someone show their own homework.

I run PickAPlugin (https://pickaplugin.com), a free hand-sorted directory of ChatGPT and Codex plugins. If the Linkly MCP server has a plugin.json I'd happily add it for free. And if you think we fit under Tier 2, a link would be great, but no pressure either way.

Aaron, PickAPlugin

subject: Your MCP directories and registries list
text:
Hi David,

Saw your top MCP directories and registries post. The 'are you looking for a server or listing one' split is a smart way to frame it.

One for the list if you think it fits: PickAPlugin (https://pickaplugin.com), a free, independent directory of ChatGPT and Codex plugins, many of which bundle MCP servers. Everything is sorted by hand and shows the install command and last update. Free listings, no account.

Aaron, PickAPlugin

subject: Your ChatGPT plugins explainer
text:
Hi Gaintage team,

Good read on how ChatGPT plugins work now. The section on how plugins use MCP servers is clearer than most I've seen.

For your 'where to find ChatGPT plugins' section: PickAPlugin (https://pickaplugin.com) is a free, hand-sorted directory of community ChatGPT and Codex plugins, with install commands and update dates. We also put out some original data at https://pickaplugin.com/research/state-of-codex-plugins-2026 that's free to cite. Might be a useful link for readers.

Aaron, PickAPlugin

subject: Your plugins vs apps vs connectors post
text:
Hi,

Your post untangling plugins vs apps vs connectors vs skills is the plain English version I wish I'd had a few months ago.

If readers want to see real examples, PickAPlugin (https://pickaplugin.com) is a free, hand-sorted directory of ChatGPT and Codex plugins, with what each one bundles and how to install it. Feel free to link it if it helps. We also have some original numbers at https://pickaplugin.com/research/state-of-codex-plugins-2026, free to cite with credit.

Aaron, PickAPlugin
